title: Add operator-silo enforcer, KMS metadata propagator, and audit-stitcher
author: Aisha Raman
release_notes: Introduces an operator-silo enforcement layer (opt-in), propagates KMS residency metadata through service boundaries, and stitches distributed audit fragments into a single canonical audit envelope. Backwards compatible; feature gated under 'operator_silo' feature flag and rollout via canary namespaces.
description: Context: Customers with strict residency and operator segregation requirements asked for a light-weight enforcement layer that prevents cross-geozone operator actions while preserving existing RBACv2 decision flow. This PR introduces three coordinated components: 1) operator-silo enforcer: a middleware that enforces operator-scoped bindings (silo tag + role) and short-circuits unsafe operator operations; 2) KMS metadata propagator: attaches minimal, signed KMS residency and provider metadata to outbound calls so downstream services can make region-aware decisions without extra RPCs; 3) audit-stitcher: a background worker that collects per-hop audit fragments and emits a canonical audit envelope with provenance and non-repudiation HMACs. Motivation: reduce customer risk when operator tokens or service accounts span regions, decrease policy evaluation complexity downstream, and provide an auditable compact envelope for compliance reviews. Compatibility: all components are feature-flagged and default to no-op; existing RBACv2 policies continue to operate when the flag is off. Design highlights: operator-silo enforcer uses attribute-driven RBAC (silo_id claim) and consults the existing policy cache; KMS propagator attaches a signed metadata header (X-RW-KMS-META) that contains region, key-alias-hash, and a short-lived signature derived from the local KMS attestor; audit-stitcher subscribes to the audit fragment topic, validates HMACs, deduplicates, and emits a single envelope to the audit sink with a provenance index. Security considerations: metadata header is minimized and HMAC-protected; we avoid embedding plaintext keys. Rollout plan: 1) unit + integration tests in CI, 2) shadow rollout in staging (operator_silo=shadow), 3) canary on 5% of namespaces with observability dashboards added, 4) full rollout after 2 weeks with no regression. Related work: references ENG-2047 for operator claims standardization and SUP-6421 incident follow-up. Checklist: - [x] RFC reviewed by security - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests against mock KMS and policy cache - [x] E2E smoke tests in staging - [x] Observability (metrics/traces) added - [x] Feature flag gating implemented

review_comments: Liam O'Connor (2024-11-13): The enforcer looks good but we should avoid sync calls to the policy cache in hot paths. Can we add a local decision cache with TTL?
Aisha Raman (2024-11-13): Added a lightweight in-memory decision cache with 250ms default TTL and metrics; pushed a follow-up commit (9a1c4e5).

Sanjay Patel (2024-11-14): KMS header format LGTM but need explicit mention in the security doc that the header is verified and dropped at external ingress points. Also request an integration test that simulates a malicious downstream trying to replay metadata.
Aisha Raman (2024-11-14): Added replay-protection test and updated docs to note header validation and stripping at external boundaries (worker_test.go + docs update).
Marina Lopez (2024-11-15): Audit-stitcher HMAC validation looks sound. Please ensure we log provenance indices at INFO and errors at WARN so compliance teams can index failures.
Aisha Raman (2024-11-15): Updated logging levels and added metrics: audit.stitcher.envelopes_emitted and audit.stitcher.hmac_failures.
Security Bot (automated) (2024-11-16): SAST check flagged a potential nil deref in metadata_attestor.go:handleSigningError. Confirmed and fixed in commit c4f7b21.
SRE Review (2024-11-17): Can you add a runtime guard to avoid worker overload (backpressure) when the audit topic spikes?
